title: Sampling-led scheduler regression playbook
content:
Purpose

A lightweight playbook for using sampling-driven probes to detect scheduler regressions (batch-formation, timeout tuning, fairness drift) before they impact production SLAs. Focus is on cheap, targeted sampling instead of full traffic replays — goal is early signal + actionable triage steps. This doc collects heuristics, experiment logs, and short recipes we can follow when alerts show subtle tail changes.

Context and motivation

- We frequently see small shifts in P95/P99 driven by changes to prefill heuristics, tiny latency increases in kernel paths, or tenant skew. Full production replays are expensive; covering long-term drift with low-cost sampling reduces time-to-detect.
- This is explicitly aligned to continuous-batching scheduler tuning: batch size distribution, timeout annealing, and fairness demotion thresholds are the usual suspects.

What we sample and why

1) Head-of-queue probe: capture first 10ms of requests that start an otherwise-idle batch; isolates flush/timeout path regressions.
2) Coalescence probe: sample the last request added to batches that meet min-batch-size (shows prefill effectiveness).
3) Demotion/priority probe: sample requests that get demoted by fairness controller (good at exposing mis-calibrated demotion thresholds).
4) KV-cache interaction probe: pair a cached vs uncached request sample to measure end-to-end difference when combined with batching.

Sampling policies

- Global low-rate reservoir: 0.05% of requests across tenants to keep overhead minimal.
- Stratified tenant quota: ensure 50–100 samples/day for top 20 tenants (by QPS) so regressions at high-volume customers aren't missed.
- Burst-aware boosting: for any lane that experiences a spike (delta QPS > 2x in 1m), increase sampling to 1% for 10m to capture behavior during stress.

Instrumentation and minimal payload

- Sample payload must be tiny: headers + timestamps at arrival, batch formation events, kernel execution times (per-layer), and final latency. No full inputs are stored.
- Each sample includes: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), arrival_ts, queue_enter_ts, batch_form_ts, batch_size_at_form, flush_reason (timeout|prefill|capacity), kernel_exec_ms, kv_cache_hit_ttfb_ms, response_ts, quantiles_snapshot (p50/p95/p99 for that batch's recent history).

Benchmarks and thresholds we use as baselines (current as of 2025-02-10)

- Baseline P95 (hosted-prod): 42ms. P99: 260ms. Small-batch penalty observed when batch_size <= 4: +18ms median overhead.
- Prefill hit rate target: 68% (measured as percent of batches that reached min-prefill before timeout).

Experiment 1 — sampling rate vs signal fidelity

Hypothesis: Very low sampling rates (<=0.01%) miss important tail events; 0.05% is sweet spot for signal vs cost.

Setup:
- Traffic: replay of 12 hours production trace on staging cluster.
- Sample rates: 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.2%, 1.0% (stratified by tenant).
- Metric: P99 detection probability for injected regressions (we injected a 30ms kernel slowdown in 3% of requests).

Results (summary):
- 0.01%: detection probability 12% (often 0 samples for affected tenant).
- 0.05%: detection probability 71% (consistent detection across runs).
- 0.2%: 92% detection. 1%: 99% detection but cost doubles.

Conclusion: keep global reservoir at 0.05% with stratified boosts — good tradeoff.

Experiment 2 — targeted probes for fairness drift

Hypothesis: Demotion probe (capture demoted requests) reveals fairness-controller miscalibration earlier than broad tail monitors.

Setup:
- Canaries: two tenants (A high-QPS, B medium-QPS) on a multi-tenant instance.
- Introduced a subtle priority threshold change that demotes 12% more requests for tenant B.
- Sampling: demotion probe enabled + global reservoir.

Observations:
- Standard P99 metric saw 8% increase after ~20 minutes.
- Demotion probe showed 24% increase in latency for demoted requests within 2 minutes.
- Root cause: priority normalization code altered epoch window, causing heavier demotion during short bursts.

Takeaway: add demotion-probe histograms to alerting rule set; they detect fairness regressions much faster.

Practical triage checklist when probe signals fire

1) Verify sample integrity: ensure batch_form_ts and flush_reason present. Missing fields frequently mean instrumentation drift — revert SDK/agent changes first.
2) Check batch_size_at_form distribution for the affected tenant: is min-prefill being missed more often? If yes, adjust prefill threshold up or add burst boosting.
3) Correlate with kernel_exec_ms: is the runtime path slower? If kernel slowdown, escalate to infra and link to PRs touching kernel selection.
4) Inspect demotion probe counts: large jump points to fairness parameter change.
5) If kv_cache_hit_ttfb_ms spikes, validate cache hotness and eviction patterns.

Alerting recipes and dashboards

- Short-lived alerts (P95 increase >=10% & demotion-probe rate increase >=20%) go to SRE on-call.
- Silent alerts (sample-based P99 drift detected but small production signal): create a ticket and set sampling boost for 1h on the affected instance.
- Dashboard widgets: per-tenant small-sample P99, batch-size waterfall, flush_reason heatmap.

Cost accounting and retention

- Sample storage target: 30 days for high-strata tenants, 7 days for global reservoir samples. 
- Sampling payload per-sample ~280 bytes compressed. At 0.05% on peak QPS (300k qps worldwide) this is ~3.8 GB/day raw. Budget set at 1.5 TB/month.

Open questions and TODOs

- Should we include a tiny payload hash of the prompt length distribution in each sample? Would help correlate prompt sizes to batch formation. (TODO: Maya to prototype simple length-hash in 2d).
- Evaluate if boosting policy should be machine-learned (predict burst windows) vs rule-based. (Experiment idea: short RNN on arrival rates to anticipate bursts.)
- Integrate sampling outputs into current regression-alert pipeline (Confluence runbook link above) — automation of ticket creation and temporary sampling boosts.

Immediate next steps

- Roll out global reservoir 0.05% in canary region for 2 weeks (Connor).
- Add demotion-probe histograms to alerting rules and set threshold for auto-ticketing (Jordan + SRE).
- Prototype prompt-length hash field and measure cardinality (Maya).

Notes to self / field diary snippets

- 2025-02-12: Small sample flagged a drop in prefill hit-rate for tenant X; turned out to be a change in tenant client-side batching config. Good catch.
- 2025-02-15: During a burst, sampling boost captured a kernel micro-pause that standard telemetry missed. We correlated it to a noisy process on the node (OOM killer logs).

References and links

- Related experiments: probe-led-scheduler-autotune-scrapbook (see GitHub references).
